object_description: two new buildings grouped around the existing main building to define a school square
geometry_property: circumferential canopy above the ground floor
design_condition: the two new buildings group around the existing main building to clearly define the school square, using the topographical edge and its level difference to embed the gymnasium

positive: The two new buildings group around the existing main building, clearly defining the school square and creating a harmonious ensemble
The replacement wing fits naturally between the residential buildings
Removing the street parking makes access to the school more attractive and safer
The topographical edge and its level difference are used to embed the gymnasium
The complex is accessed via two entrances, including a spacious forecourt and a staircase along the west facade
The main entrances are logically located on the central playground
A secondary serpentine path connects the upper playground with the lower sports fields, with a slide as a shortcut
Partial use of the edge, a natural play area and the school garden complement the open space qualities
The hybrid construction with wooden facades and pilaster-like concrete elements refers to the existing building despite its independent expression
The circumferential canopy structures the facade in an appropriate manner
Uses are sensibly distributed between the existing wing and the large new building
The gymnasium is internally accessible but has an independent entrance for clubs, with a sensibly arranged spectator gallery
The auditorium forms the heart of the new building and develops into a three-storey air space
This vertical spatial relationship strengthens the inner identity of the school
Four school clusters around the auditorium are each accessed via a studio area with an internal staircase
The studio zone has a high utilisation potential
The school floors form both a horizontal learning landscape and a vertical learning cluster
The organisation of the clusters impresses through the variety of uses, the studio atmosphere and the spatial experience
The project is characterised by careful urban planning, with a beautiful interior atmosphere and a wide range of possible uses
negative: It is questionable whether the two existing neighbouring buildings can fulfil their new role on the playground
The urban design creates a strong separation between lower and upper levels, landscape and courtyard
The side terrace is not sufficiently connected to the central playground for the two spaces to enter into dialogue
The accentuated street space at one of the village entry points is not convincing
The location and design of the parking lot in front of the classrooms is not convincing
The north facade still requires further development
The connection to the equipment rooms and the location of the trainers changing rooms still need rearranging
The interlocking slab concept appears to fail due to large recesses that severely restrict the shear flow
Even if revised it remains a costly solution, all the more so because a more ecological lightweight construction was dispensed with
The ensemble appears rather hermetic, with little invitation to walk through it
The structural principle does not have the same quality and functionality as the interior design
